findings.claim: 'The waxy cuticle on the upper surface reflects excess light at very high intensities, preventing photoinhibition of the chloroplast enzymes.'

Two options: (a) wrap the three sections and tag the matching questions, checks and flashcards, which would hide most of the lesson from Foundation students and leave a title that advertises content they cannot see; or (b) leave the article open and tag only the question items. I recommend (a) with the lesson re-titled, because the current state gives a Foundation student no signal at all. Not edited: it needs a build decision and would re-cut the narration.

summary: The same build fault as the sibling Paper 1 unit: <div class="higher-only"> was used to mean 'Biology-only'. Seven gates wrapped content that is Biology-only but assessed at BOTH tiers - the whole of the kidney lesson bar ADH, the whole of thermoregulation, the alveolar adaptations (which are not even Biology-only: 8.3 is in Combined Science), leaf adaptations, xerophytes, the tropisms and energy transfer efficiency. Six wrappers removed, one narrowed to the ADH section, and the four gates that are genuinely bold (inverse square law, commercial plant hormones, glucagon, IVF and clomifene) kept with 21 questions, checks and flashcards tagged '(Higher tier)' to match. Also fixed: a progesterone multiple-choice question whose own mark scheme admitted the key was wrong, three 9-mark questions re-typed to 6 (this board sets none), a Key Fact that named the wrong tier restriction, a leaf cuticle described as reflecting light, and an over-length description. Three ADJUDICATE items: L4 teaches adrenalin, thyroxine and the FSH/LH cycle (all bold) with no gate at all; L6's tier metadata still reads 'higher'; and the unit omits eight Paper 2 statements including core practical 8.11.
